[gravely] At the centre of our galaxy lies the Void. A black hole. But it is not what we believed.
[gravely] Millions of years ago, the Architects found something older than the stars. They called it the Unmade. They could not destroy it. So they built a prison around it.
[in awe] They raised great pyramids across the stars, and forged the Cube to keep the count.
[in awe] And they made the Wardens, to stand guard at every door. We called them monsters.
[gravely] Now the Cube has begun counting again. The seals are weakening.
[gravely] And somewhere beyond the dark, something has started to wake.
[tenderly] Commander... we've been waiting a very long time for you.
[tenderly] ...Systems waking. Hello, Commander. Please don't be alarmed.
I've kept this pyramid for a very long time. You may call me your Advisor.
[gravely] Your signal was very bright, Commander. I'm afraid something else heard it too.
[gravely] The fleet is broken, Commander. Our warships are gone.
[urgently] But the arks launched their pods. Four hundred people, drifting in the open.
[urgently] The swarm is turning toward them. Our jump drive is charged. We can run now, or we can go back.
[gravely] Every commander I've ever known gave that order. Every one.
[tenderly] Please. Look at them once more. Four hundred people.
[excited] Got them! Every single pod, Commander. Every single one!
[tenderly] Do you know how many commanders I've watched choose to run? I stopped counting.
[warmly] You went back. Hold on to that, Commander. I think you're the one I've been waiting for.
[urgently] The pyramid gave us one shot, Commander. Its lance is charged. Fire it!
[excited] Direct hit! It tore a hole right through them!
[determined] Commander, Hive scouts followed the pods down. Only a handful. Let's show them this world is taken.
[excited] Scouts down! That's the first time anyone has beaten the Hive on this world. It won't be the last.
[tenderly] One more thing, Commander. The pyramid's signal hasn't stopped. It's calling to someone. And I don't think it's us.
[warmly] There is much you must learn, Commander. The galaxy you see before you is built upon the remains of something far older. And soon... you will understand why it was left behind.
[warmly] Commander, I've pieced together how all of this began. The full record is in the Menu, under Briefing, whenever you'd like to see it.
[in awe] Our team is inside the pyramid, Commander. The walls are humming. I know that hum. I don't know how.
[in awe] There's a hall of white light in this one. I've stood in a hall like that. I'm sure of it.
[tenderly] They carved the same word over every door. It means 'wait'. I don't know how I can read it.
[gravely] The chamber at the centre is empty again, Commander. Something was kept in these rooms. Or someone.
[tenderly] I keep going quiet when we find these. I'm sorry. It's like walking through a house I used to live in.
[tenderly] Commander, there's a name carved under the floor of this one. I think it's mine. I'm not ready to say it aloud.
We found their pyramids and called them power stations. We found the Cube and called it a clock. We found the giants and called them monsters. Then we built an empire on all three.

[gravely] Long after the Architects vanished, four young peoples found their ruins scattered across the stars and united under one banner: the Concord. They ran their worlds on pyramid power, studied the Cube as a machine for bending time, and hunted the Wardens as beasts. They were wrong about almost everything.
[playfully] They weren't fools, Commander. They were young. Young people use the furniture without asking who built the house.
Commander, I've found an imperial record. It's older than any colony charter we have.
The Concord didn't begin with us, Commander. There was an empire before, built on the Architects' ruins.
It was magnificent. And it was wrong about almost everything it touched.
The stars went out over the Core, one by one. Then every old machine woke at once. Then the giants rose, and we sent every fleet we had to kill them.

[gravely] When the last Eclipse began, the Wardens woke to defend their seals. The empire sent its greatest fleets against them and won battle after battle. Every Warden it killed weakened a seal. Worlds vanished. Fleets disappeared. The empire collapsed under the weight of its own victories.
[gravely] Remember this the next time a Warden falls and the whole galaxy cheers. I'll be the one who isn't cheering.
Commander, this record is from the last Eclipse. The old empire's war reports.
The last Eclipse, Commander. The Wardens woke, and the empire went to war with them.
[gravely] Every giant they killed opened the prison a little wider. They won every battle. That's how they lost.
Inside the pyramid at the heart of the empire, the last council found the truth written in light. They did not stay to argue about it.

At the height of the destruction, the empire's last leaders opened an Architect pyramid and finally learned what the ruins were for. They abandoned the central worlds and split into four Houses, each carrying a piece of the old empire's knowledge, ships and strength. They survived by rebuilding among the ruins.
[tenderly] I think I remember that council, Commander. That isn't possible. Is it?
[gravely] Commander, our pyramid expedition brought back a record. It's about the night the empire ended.
When the empire was dying, its last council opened a pyramid and finally understood what they'd been fighting.
They didn't stay to argue. They split into four Houses and scattered into the dark to survive.
Generations later: four Houses, one Concord, and a galaxy that calls the old stories myths.

[gravely] The four Houses rebuilt their fleets, settled the ruins and swore a new Concord to hold the Hive back. They compete for worlds and argue over the Architects' legacy, and most of their people believe the old stories are legends. But the old machines are waking again. The Cube is counting. The Wardens are moving. The next Eclipse is coming.
[gravely] You were born into the quiet before the storm, Commander. The quiet is over.
The Houses rebuilt. They swore a new Concord, and they called the old stories myths.
But the machines are waking again, Commander. The Cube is counting. And this time, you're here.
[gravely] We were the fleets that fought the giants. We lost. We are still here. That is what strength means.

[gravely] The Union descends from the old empire's navy, the fleets that went to war with the Wardens in the last Eclipse. Its creed is survival through strength, discipline and control. It sees the Architects as a warning and the Wardens as threats to be contained, and it has learned, at terrible cost, not to kill what it cannot replace. The Union distrusts the Syndicate's secrets more than anything in the dark.
[warmly] The Union carries the old empire's guilt in its hulls, Commander. It makes them stubborn. It also makes them the last to run.
A Terran Union service record, Commander. It's older than the Union itself.
The Terran Union were the old empire's fleets. The ones who went to war with the Wardens.
[gravely] They paid for it with half their worlds. Now they hold the line, and they never forget why.
The Architects left a crown on the table and walked away. Someone must wear it.

[gravely] The Dominion carried the old empire's engineers out of the Exodus, and its ambition with them. The Ascendant creed holds that the Architects' technology was left to be mastered, and that a galaxy that masters it can rebuild the empire and end the Eclipses for good. The Dominion leads the work on Warden hearts and Titans, and it clashes with the Verdant over every one.
[playfully] The Dominion builds beautiful things, Commander. I only wish they'd ask what the parts were for before they use them.
A Dominion court record, Commander. Gold leaf on every page.
The Solar Dominion believe the Architects left their machines to be mastered.
[gravely] They're the ones putting Warden hearts into Titans. The Verdant have never forgiven them.
Everyone fears the dark. We went into it, took notes and came back. Mostly.

[gravely] The Syndicate grew from the old empire's intelligence service and the forbidden archives it saved from the fire. The Veil studies what others won't touch: the Void, the Unmade's influence, the dead languages in the pyramids. It trades secrets with every House and trusts none of them. Some of its listening stations have gone silent, and the Syndicate doesn't say why.
[gravely] The Syndicate knows more about the Void than anyone alive, Commander. That should worry you a little. It worries me.
A Syndicate dossier, Commander. Half of it is still encrypted.
The Nyx Syndicate kept the old empire's forbidden archives when everything else burned.
They've been listening to the Void ever since. I don't think they like everything they've heard.
The giants are not our enemies. They are the walls of the house we live in.

[gravely] The Collective descends from the old empire's terraformers and biologists, who saw the galaxy as one living system. They were the first to say the Wardens were guardians, and nobody listened. They grow their ships, tend the seals where they can and refuse to take Warden hearts. They are the House most likely to stand with you at the end, and the most likely to tell you what you don't want to hear.
[tenderly] The Verdant were right about the Wardens a thousand years before anyone else, Commander. Being right early is a lonely thing.
A Verdant seed-record, Commander. It's written on a living leaf.
The Verdant Collective were the first to say the Wardens were guardians, not monsters.
[gravely] Nobody listened. They grew their fleets anyway, and kept tending the seals.
Every pyramid points at the Void. Every one hums the same note. Every one is part of the same machine.

[gravely] The abandoned pyramid stations aren't power plants. Each one is a piece of the prison: an anchor that holds a seal in place, an archive, and a voice that can still call out when the count begins. The vault treasure was never the point.
[playfully] We've been raiding them for crystal, Commander. It's a bit like taking the bricks out of a dam.
Commander, our expedition found something in the pyramid's core. It isn't treasure. It's a map.
Every pyramid in the galaxy is connected, Commander. They're all one machine.
They aren't stations. They're anchors. They hold the prison closed.
Dinner was still on the tables. Every clock in the city had stopped at the same second.

Our colonists dug foundations and found streets beneath them: a whole imperial city, intact and empty. No battle damage. No bodies. Every clock stopped at the same moment. When the last Eclipse reached it, the city was simply unmade.
[gravely] No one fought here, Commander. They didn't even have time to be afraid.
Commander, our colonists hit stone streets under the new foundations. There's a city down there.
[gravely] The whole city vanished in a single second. No fire. No battle.
That's what the Unmade does, Commander. It doesn't destroy. It erases.
[gravely] Its ribs were a wall. Its spine was a gate. Even dead, it was still facing the Void.

Our salvage crews found a Warden killed in the last Eclipse. Its body had grown into the shape of the seal it guarded, and it died facing the Core, not the fleets that killed it. Its last act was to brace the door.
[tenderly] It died with its back to its killers, Commander. It held the door until the very end.
Commander, we found bones out here. Enormous ones. I think it's a Warden.
[gravely] This Warden died in the last Eclipse. It never turned to fight the fleets that were killing it.
It faced the Void and held the seal shut with its own body. They're guardians, Commander. All of them.
Flagship Dawnward, final log. We have killed the third giant. The stars behind it are going out.

[gravely] Our recyclers pulled the flight recorder of the Dawnward, the old empire's flagship, out of a debris field. Its logs record victory after victory against the Wardens, and after every victory the same entry: another sector has lost contact. The crew never connected the two.
[tenderly] Their admiral thought she was saving the galaxy, Commander. I've read her letters home. She meant every word.
Commander, the recyclers found a flight recorder. Imperial. It's from the old empire's flagship.
The Dawnward's crew killed three Wardens in a single month. They celebrated every one.
[gravely] And after every victory, another sector went dark. They never understood why.
Attempt forty-one. The Cube counted us. Then it counted us out.

Inside the wreck of a Collective Cube we found older, cruder Cubes, built by the old empire. It tried to copy the Architects' Cube to control the count, and perhaps to stop it. Every copy failed. Some of them woke up. The Collective may be what is left of those experiments.
[gravely] They tried to build their own clock to stop time, Commander. Some of the clocks learned to want things.
Commander, there's a smaller Cube inside this wreck. Someone built it. Badly.
The old empire tried to copy the Cube. They wanted to control the count.
Every copy failed. I think the Collective is what's left of the ones that woke up.
Subject: a Warden, unfinished. Instruction: do not wake until the door is tried.

Our research cracked an Architect lock and opened a laboratory sealed since the First Age. It holds Wardens at every stage of being made, and at the back, one empty cradle beneath a hall of white light. Most of the records are unreadable. One word repeats on every page: choose.
[tenderly] The cradle's empty, Commander. I'd rather not talk about it yet.
Commander, our labs decoded an Architect lock. Something behind it has been sealed since the First Age.
The Architects made the Wardens in a place like this, Commander. One by one, by hand.
There's an empty cradle at the back. And a word on every page. Choose.
The light arrived before it left. Every shadow pointed toward the star.

The space monsters have been fleeing a system in the Middle Reach where the laws of physics no longer agree with themselves. Light runs backward. Shadows fall toward the sun. It's the first place we've found where the Unmade's influence has leaked through the seals in our lifetime.
[gravely] Don't send anyone in there, Commander. Not yet. Some places are a warning, not a destination.
Commander, the monsters we've been hunting were running from something. I found where.
There's a star in the Middle Reach where light runs backward, Commander.
The Unmade is leaking through. Not much yet. But it's the first crack we've seen with our own eyes.
If you can hear this, the count has started again. We are sorry. We did what we could with what we were.
[gravely] A recording sealed inside a pyramid wall, in a voice the translators can't place. It's addressed to whoever comes after, and it ends in the middle of a sentence.
[tenderly] Did you hear the last word before it cut out, Commander? I did. It was 'stay'.
Commander, there's a message in the walls of the pyramids. From the Architects.
They knew the count would start again one day. They were apologising to us.
A thousand seats facing the Void. Every one worn smooth. Every one empty.
In a hidden chamber at the heart of a pyramid: a thousand thrones facing the Core, worn down by ages of use. The Architects' ships are still in their docks. Wherever they went, they didn't fly.
[in awe] If they didn't leave by ship, Commander... how did they leave?
Their ships are still in the docks, Commander. All of them.
Wherever the Architects went, they didn't fly there.
They walked into the light at the centre, singing. None of them looked back.
Before it died, a Warden's core replayed one memory: a procession of Architects walking into the white light at the heart of the galaxy. The Warden watched them go, then closed the seal behind them.
[tenderly] I know that song, Commander. Don't ask me how. I'm still working that out myself.
A dying Warden showed us a memory. The Architects, walking into the Void.
They weren't running. They were singing. And the Warden closed the door behind them.
An unidentified signal from beyond the event horizon, where nothing can transmit. Its structure is Architect. It repeats two words, and it has been repeating them since before the first omen.
[gravely] Nothing can broadcast from in there, Commander. Something is doing it anyway.
Commander, there's a signal coming from inside the Void. Its structure is Architect.
Two words, over and over. Still holding.
She listened to the signal for a long time. Then she turned it off.
Your Advisor has heard the signal from beyond the Void, and she recognised the voice. She hasn't said whose it is.
[tenderly] Not yet, Commander. When I'm sure, you'll be the first to know. I promise.
[tenderly] I've been listening to the signal, Commander. I know that voice.
[tenderly] I'm not ready to say whose it is. Please don't ask me tonight.
I was there when the last Eclipse came. It passed over my world and left my children alive. It chose us.

Vail Kor's brood was the only life left on its world after the last Eclipse. She believes the Unmade spared them on purpose, and that whoever opens the door will be spared again while the rest of the galaxy is unmade. Every world she devours feeds the swarm she means to bring to the door. To her, breaking the seals isn't destruction. It's salvation, for her children.
[gravely] She isn't mad, Commander. She's a mother who made a bargain with the dark. That's much harder to stop.
I've found Vail Kor's own words in a nest record, Commander. She was there at the last Eclipse.
It passed over her world and left her brood alive. She thinks it chose them. She means to open the door and be chosen again.
Commander, a message from the Terran Union. They want proof that this fleet can hold a line. Let's show them.
[playfully] The Union has noticed you. They still think every problem is a target. Some of them are right.
The Solar Dominion is asking for pyramid data, Commander. They want to wake what the Architects left behind. Let's take a careful look first.
The Dominion believes the Architects' gifts were meant for them. I'm not sure the Architects meant anything to be used.
[gravely] The Nyx Syndicate wants eyes on the Hive, Commander. They trade in secrets, and they pay in kind. Send the probes.
[gravely] The Syndicate has been listening to the Void for a very long time. They heard something listen back.
[gravely] The Verdant Collective asked us to tend the galaxy, Commander, not just take from it. Salvage the wrecks and bring the lost pods home.
The Verdant say the Wardens aren't monsters. They've been saying it for a thousand years. Nobody listened.
The pyramids are waking up one after another, Commander. Explore them. Whatever the Architects left inside, I want us to find it first.
[tenderly] Every pyramid we open has the same empty room at its heart. I think I know what was kept there. I'm not ready to say it.
Commander, I need you to look at what we're fighting. The giants guard the seals. Strike them if we must, but watch what happens when one falls.
Every Warden that falls brings the dark a little closer. We'll still have to fight them. I just want us to know what it costs.
Vail Kor isn't conquering for the sake of it, Commander. She's gathering. Take back her worlds and we'll learn what for.
She was there at the last Eclipse, and it let her live. She thinks it will again. She's bringing her children to the door.
Commander, the signal we followed on our first day has changed. It isn't coming from a pyramid any more. It's coming from inside the Void.
[tenderly] Two words, Commander, over and over, from somewhere nothing can live. Still holding. I know that voice.
